## Overview
Ongoing work integrating CyVerse user-facing applications with Tapis-backed HPC execution, and co-developing training materials that teach researchers and cyberinfrastructure professionals to run AI- and HPC-enabled viral ecology workflows.

## Scientific or practical problem
Powerful HPC and cloud research-computing resources (CyVerse, ACCESS, Tapis) are underused by domain researchers because the tooling and documentation gap between "has an HPC allocation" and "can run their analysis reliably" is often large.

## My role
**Cyberinfrastructure-facing bioinformatics developer.** I integrate CyVerse applications with Tapis-backed execution, manage data transfer and input/output mapping, document app-update procedures and computational protocols (via Protocols.io), and co-develop training modules and example datasets for the **iVirus Cyberinfrastructure Training Initiative**.

## Dataset or data type
Example/training datasets for viral and eco-genomics workflows (not primary research data).

## Methods and technologies
- CyVerse discovery environment app development
- Tapis-backed HPC job execution
- Data transfer and I/O mapping and synchronization
- Protocol and procedure documentation (Protocols.io)
- Training-module and example-dataset development

## Workflow diagram
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[CyVerse app] --> B[Tapis job submission]
  B --> C[HPC execution]
  C --> D[Output synced back to CyVerse]
  D --> E[Documented protocol / training module]
```

## Major results or outputs
Updated and documented viral/eco-genomics analysis applications on national cyberinfrastructure platforms; contributed training modules supporting NSF-funded pipelines and future grant development.

## Challenges and decisions
Prioritizing documentation and reproducibility (so others can maintain and extend the apps) alongside the underlying analysis correctness — treating "usable by someone else" as a deliverable, not an afterthought.
